note:
A fresh check found these problems in this version. Fix each one, and keep everything that is right:
- Question a, wording: The why says 'only checking every criterion shows these trade-offs' and 'its effects must be explained'. The card simply tells students to compare all options and explain likely effects, so 'only' and 'must' overstate it. Softer wording would fit better, e.g. 'checking every criterion shows these trade-offs'.

rejected.title: Weighing strategies with criteria
card: A strategy is a plan to deal with a problem, such as flooding or a shortage of clean water. Each option has strengths and weaknesses, so compare them all against three criteria.
Environmental
the effect on land, water, air and living things.
Economic
the cost of the option and the money it saves or earns.
Social
the effect on people's health, safety, jobs and way of life. Then recommend one option and explain its likely effects, including the downsides it still has.
rejected.remember: Compare options against environmental, economic and social criteria, then explain the likely effects of your choice.

a.q: Why should a geographer compare options against several criteria before recommending a strategy?
opts: Doing well on one criterion can hide harm on another
Using all three criteria can remove a strategy's downsides
Each criterion ranks the options in the same order
Cost decides the choice, and the other criteria are extras
a.why: An option can look good on cost but harm the environment or people, and only checking every criterion shows these trade-offs. Comparing does not remove downsides: the chosen option still has some, which is why its effects must be explained.
a.clue: Think about an option that is cheap but causes harm.

b.q: A council in Tasmania is choosing how to protect a coastal town from erosion. A sea wall costs a lot and may speed up erosion on nearby beaches. Which statement uses an economic criterion?
opts: The sea wall costs a lot to build and maintain
The sea wall may speed up erosion on nearby beaches
The sea wall would keep homes safe for residents
The sea wall would change the habitat of shore birds
b.why: Cost to build and maintain is a money matter, so it is an economic criterion. Erosion on beaches and shore bird habitat are environmental effects. Safety for residents is social, which is the tempting option because homes also have a dollar value.
b.clue: Homes are worth money, but what is that statement really about?

draft.title: Weighing strategies with criteria
card: A strategy is a plan to deal with a problem, such as flooding or a shortage of clean water. There is often more than one option, so choosing needs a fair method.
Environmental
the effect on land, water, air and living things.
Economic
the cost of the option and the money it saves or earns.
Social
the effect on people's health, safety, jobs and way of life. Compare each option against all three criteria, then recommend one and explain its likely effects, including downsides.
draft.remember: Compare options against environmental, economic and social criteria, then explain the likely effects of your choice.

a.q: Why should a geographer compare options against several criteria before recommending a strategy?
opts: An option may do well on one criterion and badly on another
The cheapest option is always the one that works best
Only one criterion can be tested with evidence
A strategy with no downsides can always be found
a.why: An option can look good on cost but harm the environment or people. Comparing against all three criteria shows these trade-offs. Cost alone is not enough, because the card says to weigh environmental and social effects too.
a.clue: Think about an option that is cheap but causes harm.

b.q: A council in Tasmania is choosing how to protect a coastal town from erosion. A sea wall costs a lot and may speed up erosion on nearby beaches. Which statement uses an economic criterion?
opts: The sea wall costs a lot to build and maintain
The sea wall may speed up erosion on nearby beaches
The sea wall would keep homes safe for residents
The sea wall would change the habitat of shore birds
b.why: Cost to build and maintain is a money matter, so it is an economic criterion. Erosion on beaches and shore bird habitat are environmental effects. Safety for residents is social, which is the tempting option because homes also have a dollar value.
b.clue: Which statement is about money spent?

a.best: An option may do well on one criterion and badly on another

b.best: The sea wall costs a lot to build and maintain

problems.detail: The right option is the only one with a hedge ('may'). All three distractors use absolutes ('always', 'only'), so a student can pick the answer by test-taking instinct without knowing the idea.
The clue 'Which statement is about money spent?' points straight at the only option that mentions cost. It removes the need to know which criterion is economic.

check.summary: The facts and the answers are sound. In question a, the right option stands out as the only hedged one against absolute distractors, and the clue for question b gives its answer away.
